## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence in the 69 docs traces to a source rule, variant value, parameter description, eligibility evidence contract or tool contract. Explanatory parentheticals ("the facility numbers its contacts against the schedule", "the surviving borrower, in care, could answer only once the death was reported", and so on) are source rule text. The hypothetical examples use generic dates and none matches a task value.
- No added confirmation, review, notification or step. No "if unmet, first call …" guidance. No task's opening world state is written as a policy fact.
- Retired surface: all eight overwrites of the difficulty (six distinct base clauses) are carried as "no longer in force". No doc retires a clause that the source never declared retired.
- Source-side finding (reported for routing; this audit does not count it as a KB defect, per Step 4):
  - **S1 — parameter description not updated by the overwrite (medium).** `parameter_schema.absence_start_basis` = "Which date starts a health-care absence (code)", value `facility_admission_date` under every plan. Since `residency_ext_absence_start_vacancy` retired the base clause, the facility admission date is only the fallback ("otherwise the facility admission date per absence_start_basis"). The facet `absence_allowances_schedule_aa45392c` renders the description faithfully but without that condition, in three places:
    - the table row "Date that starts a health-care absence | the facility admission date";
    - the Q&A line "*From which date is a health-care absence counted?* The facility admission date.";
    - the illustration "contacts fall at 90-day intervals counted from that date [the facility admission date]".
    For this task the absence starts on the departure date, 2026-01-01; the admission date is 2026-01-29. On the visible side, `health_care_absence_monitoring_f983425c` item 3 (retirement notice) and `absence_start_date_determination_c70c2079` §1 settle it, so this is not a RUNTIME RED. It is still a second statement that gives the wrong date when read alone. Class: source-side, stale parameter description vs. a declared overwrite.
  - S2 (low, untriggered): base `residency_nonoccupancy` still measures the 12-month limit "since the facility admission date", while its `anchor_source` is `absence_start_date`. After the overwrite these can differ. `nonoccupancy_confirmation_and_cure_c05b0a97` Article 2 carries both faithfully ("since the facility admission date, read as the absence start date on the profile record"). Same class as S1.
  - S3 (low, seed realism, no effect): `supporting_document` f3d89b39 has `created_at 2026-09-21` but `received_date 2026-07-27`. `created_at` serves only as a same-date tie-break, and no tie arises.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** No KB-side omission, addition, change of meaning or retired-surface error was found across the full domain, including the untriggered tiers of all 21 factors in scope. S1–S3 are source-side findings for the coordinator to route. First revision; there are no earlier revisions.

## dependency_form

- Each of the three prerequisite sentences appears verbatim and only in its blocked policy's hub, with one same-form restatement each ("Restated: …", "Equivalently: …", "Put the other way round: …"). None is restated as an action.
- Tool names: each residency hub names only its own tool (a scan of all 358 docs for `name_xxxxxxxx` tokens found no cross-naming). There is no route, checklist, ordered step list across problems, aggregated chain, contrast of wrong vs. correct reading, or FAQ that walks the chain.
- Titles are general subjects ("Borrower Check-In Confirmations During Care", "Check-Ins Confirmed by the Care Facility", "Opening Health-Care Absence Monitoring …", "Plan Reclassification After a Certifying Borrower's Death …"). The on_request hub title names its own request type. Factor titles name the rule ("Headroom Allowance for a Surviving Borrower in Care" describes the factor's general purpose, not this customer).
- Findability: in the blind pass, every depended-on document was reached with the records' own words ("death notice", "plan", "absence start date", "supporting document"/"letter", "check-in"). Every factor document was reached with the records' own words; none could be reached only through baseline wording.
- Baselines: no "unless", "adjustments may apply" or pointer. The phrases "Under the standard rule … each zero days" and "the sum of the allowances this rule sets out" are the source `baseline.rule` verbatim (observation, not a KB addition). Factor documents name only the subject of the computation they serve (for example "used in dating a completed certification cycle"), never another document or factor.
- Observation: all three check-in hubs carry the overwrite's `replaced_by` sentence "… are numbered under their own rules", naming the sibling check-in kinds. This is source base-law text that states no order or dependency between problems.
